page.layout: One printed page: running head at top centre, page number top right; one column of running text; catchword and signature at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: minus Regi neganda est, qui nullius superio-tis [?] præter Dei dictata, ut consensum obligantia agnoscam. Emori satius est sub hoc Regno Animæ meæ, qua Deo solum subjicior, Ratione & Religione me dirigente, quam inanem Regis Titulum usurpantem constrictum me ita & captivum vivere, ut nec conscientiæ nec Rationis usus permittatur, quo quid probem, quid improbem, (prout Regem decet) declarem.

Abfit enim ut illud unquam credam, Majestatem Coronæ Angliæ ita obstrictam teneri Coronationis suæ Juramento, ut in quæcunque subditorum suorum in Parlamentis postulata, cœcâ quadam & brutâ verborum Formulâ, consentire necesse habeat, quod tamen inferunt nonnulli, qui, dum hoc mihi Negativæ Vocis jus, ut Regi, eripiunt, eâdem operâ impudenter me privant omni illa Rationis, & Conscientiæ Bonæ Libertate, quâ Ipsi, & Tota Angliæ Communitas (quatenus influit in Publicum) gaudet, qui omnes ægre admodum paterentur non licere in quacunque re contradicere, quam vel Ipse ut Rex, vel mecum unâ Domus Parium, non jam amplius (si sic fieret) rogare videremur, sed exigere. Arbitror me in hoc satis fidem juramenti liberasse, cum secundum eas Leges regâ, quas Populus juxta cum Proceribus, Me ipso adsentiente comprobavit.

page.notes: Running head and page number read from the scan; the "3" of the page number is decorative and partly worn. Doubtful: "superio-tis" at the line end (the word may be superioritis, the split is unclear) and "pro-culdubio", where the printed space after the hyphen is missing. Greek running head is set in Greek capitals; the final letter reads as eta. The page ends mid-sentence: the sentence continues on the next page (Honos is the catchword). The printed hyphen in "infe-runt" is resolved as inferunt.
